name: Cybersecurity Fundamentals
description: Core security concepts such as the CIA triad, threats and controls, risk management, and secure authentication practices.

questions.question: An attacker silently changes the amounts in a company's payroll records. Which property of the CIA triad has been violated?
options: Confidentiality
Integrity
Availability
Anonymity
questions.explanation: Integrity means data is accurate and has not been altered without authorization. Unauthorized modification is an integrity violation.

questions.question: What does the principle of least privilege require?
options: All users share one administrator account to simplify auditing
Users receive full access first and permissions are removed only after an incident
Passwords must be at least 8 characters long
Users and processes get only the minimum access needed to perform their tasks
questions.explanation: Least privilege limits each account or process to the minimum permissions required, reducing the damage a compromised account can cause.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes authorization?
options: Determining what an already-identified user is allowed to access or do
Proving that a user is who they claim to be, e.g. with a password
Recording user actions in an audit log
Encrypting data so only the intended user can read it
questions.explanation: Authentication verifies identity; authorization decides which resources and actions that authenticated identity is permitted.

questions.question: Which scenario is the best example of defense in depth?
options: Relying on a single, very expensive next-generation firewall
Using the same strong password on every system
Combining a firewall, MFA, endpoint protection, patching and log monitoring so one failed control does not expose the system
Hiding the server's IP address so attackers cannot find it
questions.explanation: Defense in depth layers multiple independent controls so that the failure of any single control does not lead to compromise.

questions.question: A security team reviews centralized logs and raises an alert when unusual logins occur. What type of control is this?
options: Preventive
Corrective
Deterrent
Detective
questions.explanation: Detective controls identify and alert on events that have occurred or are occurring; they do not block them (preventive) or repair damage (corrective).

questions.question: A company buys a cyber insurance policy to cover losses from a possible data breach. Which risk treatment strategy is this?
options: Risk avoidance
Risk transfer
Risk mitigation
Risk acceptance
questions.explanation: Insurance shifts the financial impact of a risk to a third party, which is risk transfer. Mitigation would reduce likelihood or impact through controls.

practical.title: Analyze suspicious SSH log entries
practical.instructions: You are reviewing /var/log/auth.log on a lab server you administer. It contains 250 lines like 'Failed password for root from 203.0.113.45 port 51122 ssh2' within 4 minutes, followed by 'Accepted password for root from 203.0.113.45 port 51190 ssh2'. In 2-5 sentences: name the attack, identify the source, explain why the last line is worrying, and recommend at least two defensive actions.
practical.expected_output: Identifies a brute-force / password-guessing attack from 203.0.113.45, notes that the accepted login means the account is likely compromised and must be investigated, and recommends controls such as blocking the IP, fail2ban/lockout or rate limiting, disabling password or root login in favor of SSH keys/MFA, and resetting credentials.

rubric.hint: Many failed logins from one source in a short time is a brute-force (password guessing) attack.
Name the attacking source IP shown in the log lines.

rubric.description: Recognizes the successful login indicates compromise
rubric.hint: The 'Accepted password' line means the attacker likely got in; treat the account as compromised.
Recommend controls such as blocking the IP, fail2ban/lockouts, disabling root/password login, SSH keys or MFA, and resetting the password.

tasks.title: Learn the CIA triad and core security controls
tasks.description: Read the NIST Cybersecurity Framework overview and summarize its core functions. Write one real-world example each for confidentiality, integrity and availability failures.
tasks.completion_criteria: A one-page summary listing the framework's core functions and three CIA examples.

tasks.title: Complete an introductory security lab
tasks.description: Work through a beginner pre-security or cyber fundamentals path on TryHackMe. Take notes on each concept covered and the commands you used.
tasks.completion_criteria: At least two beginner rooms completed with personal notes for each.

tasks.title: Harden a Linux virtual machine
tasks.description: On your own VM, create a non-root sudo user, disable SSH root and password login in favor of keys, enable a host firewall allowing only required ports, and enable automatic security updates.
tasks.completion_criteria: A checklist documenting each hardening change with the command or config line used, verified by re-testing SSH access.

tasks.title: Write a risk assessment for a small organization
tasks.description: Pick a fictional small business, list its key assets, threats and vulnerabilities, rate each risk by likelihood and impact, and propose a treatment (mitigate, transfer, avoid, accept) mapped to NIST CSF functions.
tasks.completion_criteria: A risk register with at least 8 risks, each scored and assigned a treatment and control.
